key_insight: In large-scale experiments for GBP/USD forecasting, QNN performance depended more on circuit design choices—especially gate selection and arrangement—than on simply increasing parameter count.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical design guidance for building more accurate and noise-resilient QNNs for regression tasks, while showing that real hardware imperfections remain a major deployment barrier.
method: Grid-searched 1,368 QNN configurations across encodings, ansatzes, qubit counts, depths, and cost functions
Compared QNN forecasts against a classical BiLSTM baseline on financial time series regression
Tested selected circuits on IQM Emerald to assess hardware noise sensitivity
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated configurations, the best QNN reached an R² of 0.985 and outperformed the classical BiLSTM baseline, while hardware runs showed significant degradation from gate errors and decoherence.
watch_item: Results are case-specific and near-term quantum hardware noise can strongly reduce performance, so circuit designs may not transfer directly from simulation to real devices.
paper_title: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Quantum Neural Network Configurations for Financial Time Series Forecasting
